pages.text: A lens's power comes from its two surfaces: P = (n − 1)(C₁ − C₂), with C the curvature (one over the radius) of each, positive when it bulges toward the light. Grinding sets the curvatures; polishing then wears the surface error down, roughly exponentially with time. Below a quarter of a wavelength the image is as sharp as diffraction allows (the Rayleigh criterion).
$(thing)Set$(): Front curvature C₁, Back curvature C₂, Polishing time.$(br2)$(thing)Disturbance$(): Temperature of the shop: the glass expands, and the power drifts by ±0.2%·d.
$(thing)Limits$(): none beyond the recipe windows.$(br2)$(thing)Rate$(): Longer polishing is slower.
